title: Karl Counter-Argument: Medicare drug negotiation will stop new cures
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Medicare drug negotiation will stop new cures]

The CBO estimated the Inflation Reduction Act's negotiation would mean about 13 fewer new drugs out of roughly 1,300 over 30 years, about 1%. Meanwhile seniors save billions.

[Sources: Congressional Budget Office 2022]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Generic drugs keep prices down already
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Generic drugs keep prices down already]

Drugmakers build patent thickets to block generics for years. Humira was shielded by over 100 patents, and cheaper versions didn't reach the U.S. until 2023, years after Europe got them.

[Sources: I-MAK patent analysis]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Private insurers keep healthcare costs down
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Private insurers keep healthcare costs down]

U.S. healthcare is the most expensive in the world, and private insurers pay hospitals far higher prices than Medicare for the same services.

[Sources: RAND hospital price studies]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Medicare Advantage saves taxpayers money
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Medicare Advantage saves taxpayers money]

MedPAC estimated Medicare pays private Medicare Advantage plans substantially more per enrollee than it would spend in traditional Medicare, roughly 20% more in 2024.

[Sources: MedPAC 2024 (estimate)]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Nonprofit hospitals give back to their communities
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Nonprofit hospitals give back to their communities]

Many nonprofit hospitals spend less on charity care than the value of their tax exemptions, according to Lown Institute analyses, while some sue patients over unpaid bills.

[Sources: Lown Institute Hospitals Index, KFF Health News]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Medical debt only hits people without insurance
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Medical debt only hits people without insurance]

KFF found most adults with healthcare debt had insurance. High deductibles, surprise bills and denials push insured families into debt too.

[Sources: KFF Health Care Debt Survey 2022]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Americans are just less healthy because of lifestyle
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Americans are just less healthy because of lifestyle]

Lifestyle matters, but peer countries with universal coverage have better outcomes on preventable deaths. Access to care, poverty and stress matter as much as diet.

[Sources: Commonwealth Fund Mirror, Mirror 2024]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: U.S. infant mortality looks worse only because of how we cou
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: U.S. infant mortality looks worse only because of how we count]

Even studies using consistent definitions find U.S. infant mortality higher than peer nations, with especially high rates after birth among poorer families.

[Sources: Chen, Oster & Williams, AEJ 2016]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Native Americans already get free healthcare
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Native Americans already get free healthcare]

The Indian Health Service exists because of treaty obligations in exchange for land. It's not a gift, and Congress funds it far below estimated need.

[Sources: National Indian Health Board, IHS]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Universal pre-K doesn't work
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Universal pre-K doesn't work]

Results vary by program quality. Some studies, like Tennessee's, found fading or negative effects. But high-quality programs in Boston and Oklahoma show lasting gains. Fund quality, don't abandon it.

[Sources: Gray-Lobe, Pathak & Walters 2021, Tennessee VPK study]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Home care workers are paid fairly for unskilled work
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Home care workers are paid fairly for unskilled work]

Home care is skilled, physical, emotional work. Its median pay is roughly $16 an hour, and the job was excluded from federal minimum wage rules until 2015, an exclusion rooted in racism.

[Sources: BLS, U.S. Department of Labor 2015 rule]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Domestic workers don't need labor protections
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Domestic workers don't need labor protections]

Domestic workers were left out of the NLRA and long left out of wage laws. Several states have passed Domestic Workers' Bills of Rights to fix it.

[Sources: National Domestic Workers Alliance]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Workers' comp takes care of injured workers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Workers' comp takes care of injured workers]

Many states cut workers' comp benefits and made claims harder in recent decades. Injured workers often end up relying on public programs instead.

[Sources: ProPublica / NPR 2015]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Workplace safety is the worker's own responsibility
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Workplace safety is the worker's own responsibility]

Most workplace deaths trace back to conditions employers control: missing guards, unsafe pace, no fall protection, heat. Blaming workers lets companies skip the fix.

[Sources: BLS CFOI, OSHA]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Union membership is falling because workers don't want union
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Union membership is falling because workers don't want unions]

Surveys find nearly half of nonunion workers say they would vote for a union if they could. The gap between wanting one and having one is employer opposition and weak law.

[Sources: Kochan et al., MIT 2019]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Card check takes away the secret ballot
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Card check takes away the secret ballot]

Workers can still choose an election. Card check just stops employers from forcing a drawn-out campaign full of captive-audience meetings and threats.

[Sources: Economic Policy Institute]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: NLRB penalties are strong enough to stop union busting
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: NLRB penalties are strong enough to stop union busting]

The NLRB can't fine most employers for violations. Remedies are back pay and notice postings, often years later. That's why illegal firings stay common.

[Sources: National Labor Relations Act, EPI 2019]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Starbucks workers don't need a union because the company is
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Starbucks workers don't need a union because the company is generous]

NLRB judges have found Starbucks broke labor law many times during the campaign. Benefits can be given and taken away. A contract can't be withdrawn on a whim.

[Sources: NLRB decisions]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Amazon pays well, so workers shouldn't complain
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Amazon pays well, so workers shouldn't complain]

Pay isn't everything. Amazon has been cited by OSHA for ergonomic hazards, and workers describe punishing pace targets. A union lets workers bargain over pace, not just pay.

[Sources: OSHA 2023]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: AI will create more jobs than it destroys, so workers should
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: AI will create more jobs than it destroys, so workers shouldn't worry]

Who benefits from new technology depends on who has bargaining power. Hollywood writers and actors used strikes in 2023 to win AI protections. Others can too.

[Sources: WGA 2023, SAG-AFTRA 2023]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Port strikes hurt consumers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Port strikes hurt consumers]

Dockworkers' 2024 strike lasted three days and won major raises. Shipping companies made record profits during the pandemic. Workers asked for a share.

[Sources: ILA 2024]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Healthcare strikes endanger patients
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Healthcare strikes endanger patients]

Federal law requires unions to give hospitals 10 days' notice before striking so care can be arranged. Chronic understaffing is the daily danger nurses strike against.

[Sources: NLRA Section 8(g)]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Teacher strikes hurt kids
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Teacher strikes hurt kids]

Teachers in 2018 struck for smaller classes, counselors and school funding. Kids benefit when schools are funded and teachers stay.

[Sources: News reports 2018, Chicago Teachers Union]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Public employees shouldn't be allowed to strike
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Public employees shouldn't be allowed to strike]

Many democracies allow public sector strikes with essential-service rules. When teachers and nurses can't strike, governments can underfund schools and hospitals with no pushback.

[Sources: ILO standards]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Janus protected workers' free speech
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Janus protected workers' free speech]

The case was bankrolled by groups seeking to weaken public unions. Workers still get union representation without paying for it, which drains resources for everyone.

[Sources: Janus v. AFSCME 2018, news reporting on case funding]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: The South can't be unionized
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: The South can't be unionized]

Volkswagen workers in Chattanooga voted to join the UAW in 2024. The South has a long labor history, from coal miners to sanitation workers to farmworkers.

[Sources: NLRB 2024]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Wages are rising fast now, so workers are fine
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Wages are rising fast now, so workers are fine]

Low-wage workers saw real gains recently, but many groups' real wages only caught up after years of high inflation. Decades of lost ground haven't been made up.

[Sources: EPI, BLS]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Low unemployment means workers are doing great
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Low unemployment means workers are doing great]

Having a job isn't the same as having a good job. Millions work full time and still can't afford rent or a $400 emergency.

[Sources: NLIHC, Federal Reserve SHED]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Housing is unaffordable only because of zoning, so just dere
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Housing is unaffordable only because of zoning, so just deregulate]

Zoning reform helps supply and should happen. But markets underbuild for the lowest incomes, and new supply takes years. Tenant protections and public housing are needed alongside it.

[Sources: JCHS, NLIHC]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Wall Street landlords just provide rentals people need
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Wall Street landlords just provide rentals people need]

Large investors bought many starter homes in some metros, outbidding first-time buyers and often raising rents and fees. Housing is a need, not a yield.

[Sources: Urban Institute, Federal Reserve analyses]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Tenant protections hurt small landlords
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Tenant protections hurt small landlords]

Basic protections like notice requirements, repair standards and limits on retaliation mostly stop the worst abuses. Responsible landlords already meet them.

[Sources: National Housing Law Project]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: People with high rent are just living beyond their means
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: People with high rent are just living beyond their means]

A full-time worker needs about $32 an hour to afford a modest two-bedroom. That's not lifestyle. That's the market.

[Sources: NLIHC Out of Reach 2024]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: The mortgage interest deduction helps the middle class
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: The mortgage interest deduction helps the middle class]

Most of its benefit goes to higher-income households with bigger mortgages. Renters and lower-income owners get little or nothing.

[Sources: Tax Policy Center]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Public housing breeds crime
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Public housing breeds crime]

Crime tracks concentrated poverty and disinvestment, not public ownership. Well-funded, mixed-income public housing works in cities around the world.

[Sources: Urban Institute, City of Vienna]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Community land trusts violate property rights
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Community land trusts violate property rights]

Families choose to buy CLT homes and own them, with resale limits they agree to. It's a voluntary way to keep homes affordable for the next family.

[Sources: Grounded Solutions Network]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Housing First works in Finland but not here
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Housing First works in Finland but not here]

Houston, in Texas, cut homelessness by more than half using Housing First. It works here when it's funded.

[Sources: Coalition for the Homeless Houston]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Homeless camp sweeps solve homelessness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Homeless camp sweeps solve homelessness]

Sweeps move people without housing them and disrupt their medical care. A 2023 modeling study projected sweeps would increase overdose deaths and hospitalizations.

[Sources: Barocas et al., JAMA 2023 (modeling estimate)]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Clean water is a local problem
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Clean water is a local problem]

Flint and Jackson show what happens when poor cities are left to fail. Federal standards and funding exist because local budgets can't fix century-old pipes alone.

[Sources: U.S. EPA, Bipartisan Infrastructure Law 2021]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Replacing lead pipes costs too much
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Replacing lead pipes costs too much]

The 2021 infrastructure law set aside $15 billion for lead service line replacement. Lead harms children's brains for life. The cost of not fixing it is far higher.

[Sources: Bipartisan Infrastructure Law 2021, EPA]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Environmental justice is just identity politics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Environmental justice is just identity politics]

Exposure to pollution follows race and income. In parts of Louisiana's Cancer Alley, EPA estimated cancer risks up to about 50 times the national average.

[Sources: EPA NATA 2014]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Taxing inheritances is double taxation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Taxing inheritances is double taxation]

Much of large estates is unrealized capital gains that were never taxed at all. Stepped-up basis erases them at death. Without an estate tax, they'd never be taxed once.

[Sources: Tax Policy Center, Joint Committee on Taxation]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Carried interest rewards risk-taking
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Carried interest rewards risk-taking]

Fund managers mostly invest other people's money and earn fees either way. Carried interest lets them treat pay for services as lower-taxed capital gains.

[Sources: Tax Policy Center]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: The IRS goes after the rich too aggressively
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: The IRS goes after the rich too aggressively]

For years, low-income EITC claimants were audited at rates higher than many wealthy filers, because those audits were cheap. Budget cuts hollowed out enforcement at the top.

[Sources: TRAC Syracuse 2019, ProPublica 2019]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: IRS funding will target the middle class
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: IRS funding will target the middle class]

Treasury directed new enforcement toward households earning more than $400,000 and large corporations, where the biggest unpaid taxes are.

[Sources: U.S. Treasury 2022]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: A flat tax would be fairer
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: A flat tax would be fairer]

When you count sales, payroll and property taxes, the total system is already close to flat or regressive in many states. A flat income tax would shift even more of the load onto workers.

[Sources: ITEP Who Pays? 2024]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Corporate profits are at normal levels
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Corporate profits are at normal levels]

Corporate profits as a share of GDP reached historic highs in recent years while the labor share of income fell.

[Sources: Bureau of Economic Analysis]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Shareholders deserve all the profits because they take the r
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Shareholders deserve all the profits because they take the risk]

Workers take risks too: injuries, layoffs, closed plants and lost pensions. And diversified shareholders can spread risk in ways workers can't.

[Sources: BLS, Economic Policy Institute]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: CEOs are paid for performance
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: CEOs are paid for performance]

Research finds CEO pay tracks stock market swings and pay-setting by friendly boards more than individual performance. Pay rose to roughly 290 times typical workers' pay.

[Sources: Bebchuk & Fried, Pay Without Performance, EPI 2024]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: The EITC is enough, so we don't need a higher minimum wage
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: The EITC is enough, so we don't need a higher minimum wage]

They work best together. Alone, the EITC can let employers keep wages low while taxpayers fill the gap. A strong minimum wage puts the floor on employers.

[Sources: CBPP, EPI]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Social Security should be privatized
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Social Security should be privatized]

Privatized accounts would have taken huge losses in the 2008 crash right as people retired. Social Security's guaranteed benefit is what keeps tens of millions of seniors out of poverty.

[Sources: CBPP, Social Security Administration]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Raising the retirement age is the fair fix for Social Securi
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Raising the retirement age is the fair fix for Social Security]

Life expectancy gains have gone mostly to higher earners. Raising the age cuts benefits hardest for workers in physical jobs who die younger. Lifting the payroll tax cap asks more of those who can afford it.

[Sources: National Academies 2015, Social Security Trustees]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: 401(k)s are better than pensions
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: 401(k)s are better than pensions]

Nearly half of U.S. households have no retirement account at all. 401(k)s shift market risk onto workers, and many can't afford to contribute.

[Sources: Federal Reserve SCF 2022]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Medicare for All would destroy insurance jobs
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Medicare for All would destroy insurance jobs]

A transition plan can retrain and protect those workers. We shouldn't keep a wasteful billing industry alive at the cost of tens of thousands of preventable deaths each year.

[Sources: PERI 2018, Galvani et al., Lancet 2020]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: People on Medicaid don't work
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: People on Medicaid don't work]

Most nonelderly adults on Medicaid are working or are caregivers, students or disabled. Many work in jobs that don't offer health insurance.

[Sources: KFF]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Medicaid work requirements help people find jobs
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Medicaid work requirements help people find jobs]

When Arkansas imposed work requirements in 2018, about 18,000 people lost coverage and research found no significant increase in employment.

[Sources: Sommers et al., NEJM 2019]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: SNAP makes people dependent
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: SNAP makes people dependent]

Most people use SNAP for a limited time during job loss, low pay or family hardship. It's a bridge, and it keeps kids fed while parents get back on their feet.

[Sources: USDA, CBPP]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Puerto Ricans aren't really Americans
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Puerto Ricans aren't really Americans]

Puerto Ricans have been U.S. citizens since 1917 and serve in the military. They still can't vote for president from the island.

[Sources: Jones–Shafroth Act 1917]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Native treaty rights are outdated
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Native treaty rights are outdated]

The Constitution calls treaties the 'supreme law of the land.' In McGirt v. Oklahoma (2020), the Supreme Court affirmed that a treaty reservation still existed because Congress never ended it.

[Sources: U.S. Constitution, Article VI, McGirt v. Oklahoma 2020]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Legacy admissions reward loyal families
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Legacy admissions reward loyal families]

A 2023 study found children from the top 1% were about twice as likely to attend Ivy-Plus colleges as other applicants with the same test scores, partly due to legacy preferences.

[Sources: Chetty, Deming & Friedman 2023]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: School funding doesn't affect outcomes
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: School funding doesn't affect outcomes]

Research found a 10% increase in per-pupil spending sustained over 12 years led to more education, higher wages and less adult poverty, especially for low-income kids.

[Sources: Jackson, Johnson & Persico, QJE 2016]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: College isn't worth it, so don't fund it
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: College isn't worth it, so don't fund it]

College graduates still earn substantially more on average over a lifetime. The problem isn't college. It's the debt we put on students to get there.

[Sources: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Georgetown CEW]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Free college would just help rich kids
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Free college would just help rich kids]

Programs can target community college and public universities, where most working-class students go. Rich kids already get help through legacy, tax breaks and family money.

[Sources: Georgetown CEW, TICAS]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Counting prisoners in prison towns doesn't matter
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Counting prisoners in prison towns doesn't matter]

Counting people where they're incarcerated, often rural districts far from home, inflates those districts' populations and political power while shrinking the communities they came from.

[Sources: Prison Policy Initiative]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: American workers are the freest in the world
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: American workers are the freest in the world]

Most U.S. workers can be fired for almost any reason, have no legal right to paid vacation or sick leave, and can be bound by noncompetes. That's not freedom.

[Sources: DOL, FTC 2023]
